subject: Binomial-Poisson joint model: covariance matrix of the fixed effects

messages.author: 78f18e5a32647f45
messages.subject: Binomial-Poisson joint model: covariance matrix of the fixed effects
parts:
Dear INLA community

I have a spatiotemporal joint Binomial-Poisson model with this definition:

r_ijk  ~ Binomial (n_ijk, p_ijk )

logit⁡(p_ijk)= β_01 + β_1k1 + β_21[immune]_ijk + γ_k1*[immune]_ijk +  ν_(i1) + γ_(j1) + δ(ij1)

O_ij  ~ Poisson (N_ij,IR_ij )

log⁡(IR_ij)= β_02+  β_1k2   + β_22 [immune]_ijk   + γ_k2*[immune]_ijk + ν_(i2) + γ_(j2) + δ(ij1)

with  i = areal unit (1,...,93), j = temporal unit (1,...,16), k = age groups (1,...,8), ν_(i1) & ν_(i2) spatial structured random effect, γ_(j1) & γ_(j2) temporal structured random effect, δ_(ij1) & δ_(ij2) spatiotemporal interaction. The data are structured for a joint model fit (in a list with Y as a matrix) with the following model formula:

mod <- Y ~ -1 + intercept + age.bin * immune.bin + age.pois * immune.pois + f(idarea.all.1, model = "bym2", graph = gDIST, group = g.nu, scale.model = TRUE) + f(idperiod.all.1, model = "rw1", group = g.gamma) + f(idareaperiod.all.1, model = "iid", group = g.delta)

My questions are:
  1. Is it possible to get the covariance matrix of the linear fixed effects?
  2. If I remove all f() statements, will INLA automatically fit a joint model with only fixed effects? If this is not the case, would it be possible to fit such model in INLA?
Thank you.

Kind regards,
Yessika

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: Binomial-Poisson joint model: covariance matrix of the fixed effects
parts:
Hi Yessika,

1. You can set "control.fixed(correlation.matrix=TRUE)" in your INLA call to get correlation among fixed effects.
2. Yes, removing the f() call should give you the model with only fixed effects (not sure it's a "joint" model anymore though)

Best,
Denis Rustand
he...@r-inla.org

messages.subject: Re: Binomial-Poisson joint model: covariance matrix of the fixed effects
parts:
1. You should find correlation/covariance matrix here:
mod$misc$lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix
mod$misc$lincomb.derived.covariance.matrix

2. No, I just meant that since the two outcomes are linked through the f() components, if you only keep the fixed effects it should be similar as fitting two separate models

Best,
Denis Rustand
